context_requirements: Intact sphingolipid rheostat with sufficient sphingosine substrate
Active proliferation or survival signaling dependent on S1P
Functional autophagy machinery for nonapoptotic response
TP53 status may modulate apoptotic versus autophagic outcome
falsifiers: No decrease in proliferation-associated landmark genes at 24 h in any line
No increase in autophagy or UPR landmark genes at 6 or 24 h
No difference in response between SPHK1-high and SPHK1-low lines
Predominant upregulation of proliferation genes at 24 h

evidence.supports: SK2-selective inhibitor ABC294640 induces autophagy and nonapoptotic cell death in tumor cells
ATP-competitive SK inhibitor MP-A08 induces mitochondrial-associated apoptosis and reduces tumor growth
Dual SPHK1/2 inhibitor SKI-II inhibits proliferation and induces apoptosis in HepG2 cells
SKI II induces BCL-2-independent apoptosis in prostate cancer cells
SKI inhibits SPHK1 activity, impairs cell cycle progression, and triggers apoptosis in leukemia cells

changes: Removed ATF6, XBP1, and HERPUD1 from proximal_up: the cited abstracts report autophagy and apoptosis, not UPR activation, so these genes lack mechanistic support at 6 h.
Removed ASCC3 from proximal_up: no evidence in the abstracts links sphingosine kinase inhibition to ASCC3 induction.
Removed ATF6, XBP1, and HERPUD1 from late_up: UPR activation is not supported by the cited evidence, and these genes were not justified as late transcriptional consequences.
Kept SQSTM1, BECN1, DDIT4, TRIB3, and CHAC1 as proximal/late up because autophagy and stress-response signatures are supported by PMID 20179157 and PMID 25788259.
Kept proliferation and mitotic genes in proximal_down and late_down because SK inhibition reduces S1P-driven proliferation and impairs cell cycle progression per PMID 19036099 and PMID 28433634.
Kept apoptosis genes BAX, BID, BNIP3, and BNIP3L in late_up because apoptotic induction is supported by PMID 25788259, PMID 28433634, and PMID 17879964.
Kept line_response PC3 as strong because PMID 17879964 specifically reports SKI II effects in prostate cancer cells, while other lines have weaker direct evidence.
Kept kinetics slow and magnitude weak at 6 h/moderate at 24 h because the abstracts describe delayed autophagy, apoptosis, and cell cycle effects rather than immediate transcriptional changes.
